correctness.rationale: The connected active support and Euler imbalance condition are necessary and sufficient with loops and directed multiplicities. For one active vertex the only arcs are loops. For two, the allowed nonempty cross counts have difference 0 or ±1 and give (2z+z²)/(1−z²) per pair before the two loop factors. For three active vertices, the oriented triangle differences are (t,t,t) in the balanced case and (t+1,t,t) for one chosen open endpoint pair. The weight for any given difference f is z^|f|/(1−z²). Summing over t and removing supports with fewer than two active cross pairs gives exactly H₀ and H₁; adding arbitrary loops cannot connect a third isolated vertex. The six imbalance sectors are disjoint, and the zero matrix is counted once. The rational numerator evaluated at 1 is 7, at −1 is −3, and is 4z modulo z²+z+1. Therefore the orders at 1, −1 and the primitive cube roots are respectively seven, two and one, and none cancels. The polynomial part −2 affects only n=1. Partial fractions give a degree-six quasipolynomial for n≥2 with period dividing six; any eventual quasiperiod d allows only d-th roots of unity as poles, so the two nontrivial pole orders as roots of unity force 6|d. The leading constant and capacity follow from the pole at 1 and the fiber argument. An independent reachability replay corroborates all 15 listed counts without the Euler criterion.
residual_risks: The finite reachability check does not prove arbitrary lengths; the support decomposition is the proof.
